body.title: File a small standalone story's BUILD record beside its design doc, not under docs/epics with a raw-hash folder name
body.reproduction:
1. Route a feature through triage as `small`, which starts at a standalone `design.story` (the story's only upstream artifact is its LLD; there is no DEF and no ISSUE).
2. Approve the LLD, implement, then call `insrc_build_step` with `phase: 'validate'` and `standalone: { standalone: true, epicHash, storyId, sizeClass: 'small', ... }`.

Observed (story c4c420c22b71651e S001, 2026-10-04): the BUILD record's meta carried only workflow/epicHash/storyId/createdAt/updatedAt, with no `standalone` and no `sizeClass`. BUILD.md was written to `docs/epics/c4c420c22b71651e-E20261004c4c420c2/S001/BUILD.md`, titled "Build (plan-driven)" with "Standalone: no", while the same story's LLD.md and CR.md were in `docs/standalone/vs-code-plugin-lock-insrc-chat-E20261004c4c420c2/S001/`.

Expected: BUILD.md is written beside the LLD in `docs/standalone/vs-code-plugin-lock-insrc-chat-E20261004c4c420c2/S001/`, the record is marked standalone with its size class, and it renders as a standalone build.
body.rootCause:
The standalone validate branch knows it is serving a standalone story but discards that fact before the record is written. `handleStandaloneValidate` receives the caller's standalone context (including `sizeClass`) and passes only `{ epicHash, storyId, taskId }` into the shared `runValidateSession`. That shared persist then re-derives the route with `inheritedStandalone(repoPath, epicHash)`, which reads `readEpicDefinitionCore`. `readEpicDefinitionCore` looks at exactly two artifacts, the DEF and the ISSUE; a triage-routed small story has neither, so it returns an empty object and `standalone` is undefined. The record is therefore written without a `standalone` key and without `sizeClass`.

With `standalone` not true, `buildRecordFolderArgs` takes the epic branch: `workItemKind` becomes 'epic' (so the top-level folder is docs/epics), and the slug comes from the same empty definition lookup, so it is undefined and the path builder falls back to the epic hash as the folder label. `buildRecordFolderArgs` does know how to read the standalone LLD for the anchor and label, but only on the branch taken when it has already been told the story is standalone.

The earlier fix for this symptom (commit bc157a5) replaced an omitted flag with this definition-head lookup, which resolves ISSUE-anchored (bugfix) and DEF-anchored stories but not an LLD-only one. `completion-record.ts` uses the same `inheritedStandalone` lookup and has the same gap. The record's renderer titles on `meta.sizeClass`, which is why the missing size class also produces the "plan-driven" title.
body.fixIntent: A BUILD record for a standalone story must be recognised as standalone and filed in the same folder as that story's other artifacts on every route, including the LLD-only small route. The route and size class the caller supplies to a standalone validate must reach the persisted record, and the route lookup shared by the validate and completion writers must resolve an LLD-only standalone story instead of returning nothing. The existing guarantees stay: only an explicit true is ever written for `standalone`, a prior true is never flipped by a later write, and DEF- and ISSUE-anchored stories resolve exactly as they do today. Tests must cover the first write for an LLD-only standalone story and assert the resulting BUILD.md path sits beside the LLD.

feedback.author: claude-opus-5.5 (controller)
feedback.comment:
ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE: two more variants of the same misfiling, both observed on 2026-10-04 while building the fix for ISSUE-605c70574633ed67 (an ISSUE-anchored small bugfix built with sizeClass 'trivial'). Filed here rather than as new issues because the fault is the same: a writer derives the work item's folder from something other than the item's own definition and siblings, so its record lands in a second folder.

VARIANT 2 - BUILD record, wrong DATE segment. The implement and validate turns wrote BUILD.md to docs/standalone/bug-docs-review-pane-s-opendoc-E20261004605c7057/S001/, while the ISSUE (created 2026-10-01) sits in docs/standalone/bug-docs-review-pane-s-opendoc-E20261001605c7057/. This record DID carry standalone:true and sizeClass, and the slug was right; only the E<date> anchor differed. The record's meta.createdAt was 2026-10-04T09:40:27Z. Reading buildRecordFolderArgs in src/workflow/storage.ts: on the standalone branch the anchor comes from the story's LLD and falls back to the record's own createdAt; a trivial-sized bugfix has no LLD, so the anchor is the build's own clock rather than the ISSUE's createdAt. The label on that same branch IS read from the definition head, which is why the slug was correct and only the date forked. Not verified by a test.

VARIANT 3 - code-review record, wrong top-level folder and raw-hash name. insrc_code_review_step for the same story wrote CR.md to docs/epics/605c70574633ed67-E20261004605c7057/S001/CR.md: epics instead of standalone, the epic hash instead of the slug, and today's date instead of the issue's. This matches the symptom of the original observation in this issue but on the code-review writer, not the BUILD writer, and for a story that HAS a definition head (the ISSUE). The cause was not traced in the code; ISSUE-b2e16601ad94f39b records that the CR writer takes its label from the LLD's stored meta, and with no LLD that would be empty, which is consistent with this but unconfirmed.

Both records were moved by hand beside the ISSUE in commit 82e070b.

Scope note for whoever picks this up: the original report covers an LLD-only story with no definition head; these two cover a definition-head story with no LLD. A fix that only teaches the lookup to fall back to the LLD would not cover variants 2 and 3.

citations.quotedText: return runValidateSession(repoPath, prompt, { epicHash, storyId, taskId: storyId }, summary);
as first written: meta = { workflow: 'build', epicHash, storyId, createdAt, updatedAt } with no standalone and no sizeClass
